title: Meeting Rooms II
summary: Find the fewest meeting rooms needed so that every meeting gets a room for its whole duration.

tests.explain: From 10 to 11, [9, 12] and [10, 11] run together. At 11, [10, 11] ends just as [11, 13] starts, so that room is reused. Never more than two meetings run at once.
The meetings never overlap, so one room is enough.
At time 4 all four meetings are running, so each needs its own room.

hints: The answer is the largest number of meetings running at the same moment. When can that number change?
Only at start and end times. Sort all starts, sort all ends separately, and sweep through time: a start needs a room, an end frees one.

Walk both sorted arrays with two pointers. If the next start is before the next end, a room is taken (count + 1); otherwise a room is freed first (count - 1). Process an end before a start at the same time. Track the maximum count.

complexity.time: O(n log n): sorting the start and end times
complexity.space: O(n) for the two sorted arrays
